title: The Microscope and Cells
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: The Microscope and Cells Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The compound microscope is used to observe cells; the cell theory; plant and animal cells and their organelles. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 2: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Life Science): the cell theory, parts of a cell, plant and animal cells, microscopes and cell investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All living things are made of cells.
key_sub: The nucleus controls the cell; the membrane controls what goes in and out; plant cells also have walls and chloroplasts.
body_html:
How to think about it

The cell theory: all living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and cells come from other cells.

  • Animal and plant cells: nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, vacuoles.
  • Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large vacuole.
  • Total magnification = eyepiece × objective (10× × 40× = 400×).
Example

A microscope has a 10× eyepiece and a 4× objective. What is the magnification?

10 × 4 = 40

Answer: 40×

Example

Which organelle makes food in plants?

it contains chlorophyll

Answer: the chloroplast

Common mistakes

  • Thinking only animals are made of cells.
  • Mixing up the cell wall and the cell membrane.
  • Adding the two magnifications instead of multiplying.

items.q: A microscope gives a total magnification of ×100 with a ×10 eyepiece. What is the objective magnification?
